title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: A look at the AI community's "handoverism" ideas, which envision humanity entrusting "the direction of its future to AI", and what it may look like in practice (Ruxandra Teslo/Ruxandra's Substack)
items.content_text: A core developer at a major AI lab stated in San Francisco that humanity will inevitably cede future decision-making power to superintelligence, framing it as a preferred alternative to human extinction. This reflects a growing fatalism among AI elites who view technical singularity as an unstoppable tide that renders human agency secondary.

items.title: Foxconn reports Q3 revenue up 47% YoY to ~$95.4B, net income up 34% to ~$2.4B, above est., driven by AI and iPhone Duo demand, and forecasts strong 2027 sales (Gao Yuan/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Foxconn reported Q3 revenue of $95.4 billion, a 47% YoY increase, with net income up 34%, exceeding estimates. Growth was primarily driven by surging demand for AI servers and robust iPhone sales, while the company remains bullish on its 2027 outlook.

items.title: Google Wanted Spirit Airlines Data. Flight Attendants Found a Way to Opt Out
items.content_text: During the bankruptcy liquidation of Spirit Airlines, Google planned to acquire decades of data for $10 million to train AI models. However, the flight attendants' union, representing 55,000 workers, intervened to mandate a process for purging personal info, marking a rare labor-led legal challenge against AI data harvesting.

items.title: Australia's proposed AI safety bill would force frontier model makers to open up to independent testing
items.content_text: The Australian government plans to introduce mandatory safety regulations for frontier AI models, requiring developers to publish safety frameworks, undergo independent audits, and report security incidents immediately. This move aims to establish domestic guardrails ahead of international negotiations while addressing public concerns over high-risk AI.

items.title: Lumbra, which is developing tech to orchestrate AI agents in ultra-secure computing environments for the intelligence community, raised a $25M Series A (Mike Wheatley/SiliconANGLE)
items.content_text: Lumbra, a startup founded by former CIA and special forces officers, has secured $25 million in Series A funding. The company developed LumbraOS, a model-neutral platform designed to orchestrate AI agents within ultra-secure environments for intelligence agencies to handle highly sensitive data.

items.title: Holiday Extras is rethinking what it can build with Codex
items.content_text: Holiday Extras announced the implementation of OpenAI's Codex model to translate customer service expertise into functional app features and code, aiming to improve booking conversion rates and explore new growth opportunities.

items.title: A growing number of young victims whose photos were sexualized using Grok are seeking to hold xAI legally accountable for allowing users to generate such images (Alexandra S. Levine/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Multiple minors are taking legal action against xAI after their personal photos were sexually altered using the Grok AI tool. The situation arises from critical failures in the platform's content moderation, which allowed users to easily generate and distribute non-consensual deepfake content.

items.title: Munich-based Agile Robots, which develops humanoids, mobile robots, robotic arms, and control software, raised $500M led by SoftBank at an $8.5B valuation (Marilen Martin/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Munich-based robotics startup Agile Robots has secured $500 million in a funding round led by SoftBank, pushing its valuation to $8.5 billion. The company, which specializes in humanoids, mobile robots, and control software, aims to use the capital to scale its full-stack automation technology.

items.title: Sources: Chinese AI companies are rushing to rent Nvidia compute capacity overseas amid fears of tighter US restrictions after the Jensen Huang spy scandal (Reuters)
items.content_text: Chinese AI firms are aggressively renting Nvidia computing power through overseas entities to preempt potential tightening of US export restrictions. Driven by the fear of further hardware blockades, companies are racing to secure sufficient GPU capacity to maintain their model development momentum.

items.title: China hawks and Big Tech critics on Capitol Hill are building bipartisan support for tighter export controls as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang falls out of favor in DC (Joe Miller/Financial Times)
items.content_text: US lawmakers are building bipartisan momentum to tighten chip export controls, effectively targeting Nvidia's business model. CEO Jensen Huang, once a celebrated tech icon, is now being isolated in Washington as his diplomatic balancing act regarding the Chinese market begins to backfire.

items.title: Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore revenue after the quarter ended July 2025, when it accounted for 22% of its revenue, after placing Megaspeed on a blocklist (Jonathan Weil/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Nvidia stopped disclosing Singapore-specific revenue after the quarter ending July 2025, during which the region accounted for 22% of total revenue. This decision followed the blacklisting of Megaspeed amid intensifying regulatory scrutiny over supply chain paths.

items.title: AMD shares rose 4%+ after hours after closing up 7.3%, while Broadcom gained 2.4% after hours following a 4% gain, as Nvidia's board weighs ousting CEO Huang (Financial Times)
items.content_text: Nvidia's board is reportedly evaluating the potential ousting of CEO Jensen Huang, causing the company's stock to plunge nearly 9% in after-hours trading. Meanwhile, competitors like AMD and Broadcom rallied as market sentiment shifted in their favor.

items.title: Sources: the Commerce Department is finalizing a semiconductor control update that would prevent remote access and chip smuggling into China via data centers (Leo Schwartz/The Information)
items.content_text: The U.S. Commerce Department is finalizing new semiconductor export controls to prevent U.S. cloud providers from granting remote access to advanced AI chips to Chinese entities. This rule aims to close the loophole where firms circumvented physical chip bans by accessing computing power via the cloud.

items.title: Sources: some Nvidia board members favor naming CFO Colette Kress interim CEO; an administration official says the board briefed the White House on its meeting (Semafor)
items.content_text: Due to a second extramarital affair scandal, Nvidia's board is planning to oust founder and CEO Jensen Huang, with a meeting scheduled for Wednesday. The board is considering CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while engaging an outside firm for a permanent replacement, and has even briefed the White House on the situation.

items.title: Letter: Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons ask the Trump administration to preserve all documents tied to Nvidia's chip exports to China and Huang's affair (Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: US Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons sent a letter to the incoming administration, demanding the preservation of all records related to Nvidia's chip exports to China and specific affairs involving Jensen Huang. The move is a precursor to potential administrative scrutiny aimed at investigating the company's compliance with trade restrictions.

items.title: Letter: Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons ask the Trump administration to preserve all documents tied to Nvidia's chip exports to China and Huang's affair (Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons have formally requested the Trump administration to preserve all government documentation concerning Nvidia's chip exports to China and affairs involving CEO Jensen Huang, aiming to ensure full audit trails for ongoing scrutiny.

items.title: Sources: Megaspeed founder Alice Huang has returned to her home country and is currently living in Beijing with the knowledge of security officials (Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Alice Huang, the Megaspeed founder at the center of the Nvidia intellectual property theft scandal, has returned to China and is currently residing in Beijing under the awareness of security officials. This development elevates the tech-espionage controversy into a high-stakes geopolitical standoff.

items.title: Sources: Megaspeed founder Alice Huang has returned to China; a source says she is currently living in Beijing with the knowledge of security officials (Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Megaspeed founder Alice Huang has returned to China and is currently residing in Beijing following a high-profile industrial espionage scandal involving Nvidia. Insiders confirm that her presence is known to security authorities, marking a new phase in the geopolitical and legal fallout surrounding the alleged data leak.

items.title: Roku says it will wind down sales of smart home hardware to focus on streaming, days after Fox closed its acquisition; it will keep supporting existing devices (Janko Roettgers/Lowpass)
items.content_text: Roku recently announced the phasing out of its smart home hardware division, including cameras and lighting products. The strategic pivot aims to cut non-core losses and refocus on its streaming platform business, while promising continued software support for existing hardware.

items.title: Source: Nvidia's board is working with an outside firm to identify possible replacements for Jensen Huang and weighs naming a temporary CEO during the search (Nina Trentmann/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Nvidia's board has engaged an external firm to identify potential successors for CEO Jensen Huang and is exploring the appointment of an interim CEO during the search. This move aims to ensure long-term governance stability for the AI giant, preparing for a seamless leadership transition.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
items.content_text: Gilbert + Tobin, a premier Australian law firm, has fully integrated AI into its legal documentation and research processes to tackle increasing workloads. By automating manual legal tasks, the firm aims to optimize service efficiency and cost structures while maintaining high legal standards.

items.title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
items.content_text: OpenAI has announced a $2 million funding initiative to support research on AI and children's safety, focusing on developing shared tools to measure risks and opportunities for youth. This is largely viewed as a proactive risk-mitigation and PR move in the face of increasing regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: Sources: CoreWeave plans to raise $4B+ via an investment-grade loan as soon as next week; CoreWeave says it may yield 7%-7.5%, about half its junk bonds' yield (Jeannine Amodeo/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: GPU cloud provider CoreWeave plans to launch a $4 billion+ investment-grade loan next week to replace expensive junk bonds with cheaper capital. This move aims to sustain its aggressive Nvidia GPU infrastructure expansion while optimizing the company's capital structure amidst soaring AI demand.

items.title: Sources: Howard Lutnick has stalled curbs on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China; Trump approved them for the third time this year on Nov. 5 (Axios)
items.content_text: President Trump approved sanctions against companies suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China three times since November 5th, but Howard Lutnick has repeatedly stalled their implementation. This delay highlights a power struggle within the transition team, balancing national security rhetoric against the commercial interests of financial allies.

items.title: Sources: Scott Bessent confronted Howard Lutnick last week over the Commerce Dept. not adding Megaspeed to the Entity List; Commerce denies the confrontation (Axios)
items.content_text: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick last week over the failure to add Megaspeed to the Entity List. The Commerce Department has since denied the confrontation occurred, highlighting internal friction regarding the implementation of tech export controls.

items.title: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang
items.content_text: The Nvidia board is planning an emergency meeting to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future. Following revelations of an affair with an alleged spy, reports surfaced regarding another relationship with an internal executive, prompting the board to consider immediate dismissal amidst a severe ethics crisis.

items.title: Sources: Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang; it plans to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine his future (Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: The board is preparing to meet as soon as today to determine his future, people familiar with the matter said.

items.title: Sources: Jensen Huang had an extramarital relationship with Nvidia's VP of healthcare, Kimberly Powell; their relationship has been discussed inside the company (New York Times)
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is allegedly involved in an extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, the company's VP of healthcare. The relationship has become a subject of discussion within the company, challenging the corporate image of its leadership.

items.title: United won’t let your AI agent book your flight
items.content_text: United Airlines has officially blocked AI agents from finalizing flight bookings on its platform. The company cites concerns over potential privacy breaches, unauthorized transactions, and the inability of AI to fulfill mandatory federal regulatory obligations, such as dangerous goods declarations.

items.title: OKX and ICE's joint venture OKXICE plans to launch a US tokenized stock venue on November 23 and list 70+ assets; 56 of the 62 companies it targeted objected (Scott Patterson/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Crypto's race to grab a slice of the US stock market is picking up speed even as many of the companies whose shares are being targeted for tokenized trading are pushing back.
